text:
On June 21, 1974, the Policy Committee of the Chicago Area Transportation Study adopted the 1995 Transportation System Plan. The 1995 System Plan includes all modes (public transportation, highways, aviation and freight).
On November 21, 1974, the Northeastern Illinois Planning Commission adopted the 1995 Transportation System Plan as one of its functional plans. This plan replaces the Interim Transportation Plan and Program, a composite of official public transportation plans for an area covering the eight county bistate metropolitan area. (See Exhibit "30", pages II-4 to II-6.
The Transit component of the 1995 Transportation System Plan consists of:
1. Radial Rail Network
2. Rapid Transit
3. Corridor of High Accessibility
4. Regional Bus
5. Transportation Center
6. New Local Transit Service
Within the Transit component, a regional bus is described between Joliet, Illinois and Valparaiso, Indiana via U.S. 30. This service is not intended to accommodate local circulation within suburban communities.
The <u>Highway</u> component of the 1995 Transportation System Plan consists of:
Freeways
   New Full Controlled Access Facilities in the Region
3. Corridor of High Accessibility
4. Arterial Network
Within the Highway component, U.S. 30 is shown as an arterial from the DeKalb-Kane County line near Hinckley, I'linois to the Porter-LaPorte County line near Wanatah, Indiana. The arterial network supplements the freeway system as described in this component.
Therefore, at the present time and for the near future, U.S. 30 stands as the most feasible mode for the movement of people, goods and services. In addition, this facility would serve the future regional bus trips as defined in the transit component.
